_about: Rule data for tools/checks/taste-shotcards.page.mjs: advice per shotcard category (tools/shotcards/<category>.js) and per helper. A film that calls KIT.shotcards.<helper> gets that helper's tips and, once, its category's advice. Edit the data, not the check.

categories.camera: Camera cards: one camera move at a time, eased at both ends (taste `motion` flags a dead stop or a jump), and hold the last pose for half a second so the viewer can read it.
categories.opening: Opening cards: the title must be readable (contrast 4.5:1, 3:1 for large text) before the first cut, and nothing else should compete with it in the first 2 to 3 seconds.
categories.outro: Outro cards: end on the logo or call to action and hold it still for at least 1 s (aesthetic rule R1); taste `pacing` only worries when nothing moves for more than 4 s.
categories.transition: Transition cards: one transition per cut, and one type for the whole film; start it on a beat (KIT.snap) so the cut lands with the music.
categories.dissolve: Dissolve cards: a texture dissolve is a cut that takes about a second; do not run two at once, and keep the incoming scene's first words clear of the dissolving edge.
categories.rhythm: Rhythm cards: cut on the beat with KIT.snap or W(), never with hard-coded seconds; keep the count of whole-frame hits (shake, crash zoom) at three or fewer (aesthetic rule R4).
categories.typography: Typography cards: no more than about 6 words per second of voice-over (taste `pacing`), contrast 4.5:1, and keep the text inside the title-safe box.
categories.ui-entrance: UI entrance cards: let the last item land and then hold 1 s; do not enter more things than the voice-over names, and keep the stack inside the title-safe box (taste `empty` flags a cramped frame).
categories.data: Data cards: made-up numbers need the "Illustrative data" label (the `illustrative` gate fails without it); animate the number on the word that names it.
categories.effects: Effect cards: use one hero effect per shot (taste `balance` and `empty` notice a frame it dominates), and treat glows, sheens and ripples as ambient, not as the point.
categories.interaction: Interaction cards: show one action at a time, leave a beat between the action and its result, and mock every write (never a real publish, pay or send).

tips: Taking pose times from fixed seconds: use `V()`, `W()` or `KIT.snap()` so the flyover follows the script.
Putting the cursor outside the filmed layer: it is a child of `layer`, in layer px, and tilts with it.
Zooming a focus near the edge: the start frame then crops the layer; give the layer a bleed floor (recipes/push-in.md).
Dimming siblings with your own code as well: the helper owns their `opacity`.
Making the terminal a different size from the frame: put it in `layer` and let the layer be frame-sized, so the tour numbers stay meaningful.
Wrapping long lines: `white-space: pre`, and size the box for the longest line.
Making `dur` shorter than about 1.6 s: the cruise part vanishes and it reads as one long ease.
Picking a `target` near the end of the list: the rows below it are missing, so the landing row sits low. Keep a few rows after the target.
Passing an image element that is already in the DOM elsewhere: it is moved into the layer.
Leaving the divider at 0 or 1 at the end: half the picture disappears. Rest it near the middle.
More than a few hundred dots: use bars instead.
Forgetting the "Illustrative data" label on made-up numbers (the `illustrative` QA gate fails the build).
A `value` very close to `max`: the spring overshoot swings the needle past the end of the dial.
Using the tape for a range of thousands of ticks: raise `step`.
Even spacing for uneven dates: the strip is evenly spaced (`spacing`); put the real dates in the labels, not in the distances.
More than about 7 events: the dwell time per event gets too short to read.
Loading `shotcards/dissolve.js` before `transitions.js`: it throws (`KIT.transition` is missing).
A `to` layer with its own clip-path: the transition owns it.
Different `seed` per transition in a film, or every wipe has the same edge.
A paper colour close to the scene colour: the lip disappears.
`feather: 0`: a hard wipe (`KIT.transition('wipe')`); the factory refuses it.
A glow colour on a light scene: screen blend vanishes on white; use a darker colour or `mix-blend-mode` on your own overlay.
Colour streaks on a white scene: invisible. Use a dark `from` or a coloured `color`.
Adding `KIT.cue(at, 'glitch')` is not automatic: pass `cue: 'whoosh'` to `KIT.transition` if you want a sound.
Setting `text` longer than about 24 characters: the per-letter stagger makes it last over a second.
Putting other content in the same box: the headline sits above the panel.
Three or more inks at full strength: multiply of all of them is near black. Two inks plus a pale third read better.
A dark film background: multiply needs a light ground, which the helper draws (`paper`); fade it in over your scene.
Fewer than 4 items: the scan has nothing to reveal.
Setting `dur` below about 1 s: the rows arrive in a blur.
Palettes as `hsl()` or names: use hex strings (the mixer parses `#rrggbb`).
Text over the bloom's peak: it washes out for about half a second; keep the headline off the beat.
Readouts that are real data: they are decoration. Label real numbers with a `Source:` credit elsewhere.
More than three readouts: the column crowds the top-left bracket.
Orb colours as names: they go into a `radial-gradient`, hex or `var(--kit-…)` is fine.
Hopping faster than 0.5 s per arc: the ring on landing does not finish.
Setting `transform` on `el` yourself: the helper overwrites it every frame.
Morphing icons that are images: `a` and `b` take text or HTML glyphs; for images pass `` HTML.
`shakeEl` set to the stage itself: shake a child scene wrapper, or the frame edges show.
Hits closer than 0.15 s: the pops merge and the count looks like one jump.
Putting the spotlight under the content: it is an overlay, so add it after the scene.
`dim` above 0.9: the rest of the frame disappears.
More than about 10 chips: they overlap on the ring. Use two radii (`radialWave`).
Passing `phone` as an element that has its own `transform` animation: it is left alone, so it will not pulse with the ripple.
A `rect` that is tiny (under 100 px): the corner marks overlap.
Scanning something you also zoom with the camera: pass the rect in post-zoom pixels.
A callout target outside the safe box: it is clipped by social-app UI on 9:16.
Long labels: the pill grows right; keep it under 28 characters.
Three slams in one scene: the second and third do nothing. One per scene.
`shakeEl` on the stage root: shake a child wrapper.
Passing image URLs that need the network: use local files (the `no-network` QA gate).
A `corner` outside 0..1: the light starts outside the box and the reveal looks late.
A cyclic graph with unreachable nodes: a node with no path from node 0 never appears (its arrival is `Infinity`). Connect everything to node 0.
Dozens of nodes: the cascade takes depth × `hop`.
Hard-coded colours in the scene: only `var(--kit-*)` colours change in the second copy.
Building the scene with ids: the copy duplicates them; use classes.
Running envelope.mjs on the final mix: use the voice file, or the bars follow the music too.
Forgetting `at`: the envelope starts at t = `at`; give it the line's start time.
Cursor paths that cross text you need to read: cursors are drawn on top.
Real people's names for fictional users: use first names that are plainly examples.
`every` shorter than 1 s with long body text: the card changes before it is read.
Different content heights: the cards are all the same size; keep body text to two lines.
A selection list that is not in time order: it is read in order and later times win.
Very long segment labels: they are clipped to the segment width.
A query that matches nothing: the list ends empty. Keep at least one row matching the full query.
`cps` above 10: the rows collapse faster than the eye follows.
Colours as CSS names or variables: `#rrggbb` only (they are blended in JS).
Real data: pass your own heights by editing the module's `bars`; the recipe's heights are decoration.
An animated `source`: the clones are snapshots. Shatter a still title card, or hold the animation first.
Creating the helper before the card is laid out: clone after fonts and layout are in place.
Putting the mark inside the goo group: it would melt. Draw it above.
Using it for more than about 14 blobs: it turns into a cloud; raise `r` instead.
Rows with their own transform animation: the helper owns their `transform`.
Calling before fonts load: the heights are measured at the first `set`; build the helper after layout.
Icons that are already gray: grayscale does nothing visible; use coloured SVG.
`t1 - t0` shorter than `dur`: the helper throws (no room to stagger).
A tween in CSS `transition`: not seekable; this is a function of t.
Setting `letter-spacing` elsewhere on the element: the helper owns it, with `padding-left`, opacity, transform and filter.
Putting satellites inside the nucleus element: they are positioned in the stage, not in the nucleus.
`drift` > 0 means the film never holds still after `t1`; set 0 for a still end.
A hero off the focal point: the spotlight stays at the screen centre, so the disc would miss the card.
Going past z 2.6 on bitmap art: it softens.
A video as the media: `background-clip: text` takes images and gradients, not `<video>`; use a poster frame.
Text longer than the box: it is `white-space: nowrap`; size `w` for it.
Sizing logo and word with transforms: `offsetWidth` ignores them, so size with width/height or font-size.
Leaving the wordmark visible before `t0`: the helper hides it until its clip opens.
`reps` too small for a long gap or a small font: the row runs out before the frame edge; raise it (default 16).
A CSS `@keyframes` marquee: not seekable.
More than about 12 reps on a 16:9 frame: they overlap; use two rings (two helper calls).
Using real user avatars: they are the user's media; do not fetch them at render time.
Items nested in transformed parents: `offsetLeft` is then not stage px; pass `{ el, dx, dy }`.
Running it on the real UI recording: it moves elements, so use it on the mock UI layer.
A logo with no `parts` and no `logo`: the morph ends on an empty disc; pass at least one.
Doing both on one element: they own the same transforms.
Beat times from `Math.random` or a clock: derive them from `KIT.snap` / `KIT.beat` / `V()`.
Fewer beats than items: the helper throws.
Content wider than its panel: panels clip (`overflow: hidden`); fit the media with `object-fit: cover`.
A panel border from the theme: the default is a 3 px x K.u ink border; override on `panels[i].el`.
Sub-scene text at a quarter of the frame is small: use big type in the sub-scenes (the PLAYBOOK size floor applies after scaling).
Sharing one `KIT.stage`-parented helper between cells: pass `parent: quad.cells[i].inner`.
Easing between the framings: that makes it a camera move, not a jump cut.
More than three cuts a second: it stops reading as rhythm.
Stepping the camera too: it looks like dropped frames, not style.
`KIT.easing('steps(n)')` quantises progress inside a tween; this quantises time across the shot. Use whichever matches the intent.
More than one slam in a bumper: the second one is a repeat, not an escalation.
Text sizes are set for 16:9; override per step with CSS on `.kit-bumper-text` for 9:16.
A glyph with no counter (an L): aim at the middle of a stroke and let `r` be the stroke's half-height.
Wrong (x, y): the circle opens beside the glyph; measure the counter from the real layout.
Calling `cardFlock` per frame: the sim is built at creation; build it once.
A `t1 - t0` under about 0.8 s: the cards do not settle before the blend.
Expecting two-sided paper: past 90 degrees the back face is hidden, not drawn.
A `from` with its own 3D transform: the transition owns it.
Using `versusSlam` on scenes with important text near the seam: it crosses the middle.
Photosensitivity: the burn and the slam flash are strong; keep them to one per film and short.
More than 3 columns on 9:16: they get too narrow; the width is `min(0.9·W/n, 420)` px.
Uneven column lengths: shorter columns end higher; pad or split.
Animating `font-size` on a long paragraph: it relays out every frame. Use it for one line.
Colours as names: the mixer reads `#rrggbb` or `[r, g, b]`.
More than 5 steps: the ring repeats and bores. Count from 3.
An exit word longer than 8 letters: the pieces scatter off screen before it is read.
A `gap` longer than `travel`: only one word is ever on screen. Overlap them.
Text the viewer must read: it flies for under two seconds. Use a kinetic layout for sentences.
Setting `color` on the words yourself: they use `background-clip: text`; the text colour is transparent.
Colours as `hsl()` with spaces: they go into a gradient string; hex and `var()` are safe.
Building before the font is ready: the lead lands in the wrong place. Wait for `document.fonts.ready` or build in the film's load step.
A lead word wider than the frame at 3.2×: lower `zoom`.
Very thin fonts: the 3 % outline vanishes. Raise `strokeW`.
Needs a stroke colour that differs from the background (`stroke`).
Building before fonts load: the pill is sized for the fallback font.
`every` below 0.5 s: the roll never rests.
Chips with one word: they have nothing to roll; use two or more.
Setting a fixed `width` too narrow for the longest word.
Long text on a short path: the end is clipped. Measure with `path.getTotalLength()` if unsure.
`by: 'word'` on a single word: nothing to stagger.
`fall` under 0.5 s: the bounces are too fast to read.
`drop` larger than the frame: the letters start off screen and the first part is dead time.
A static font family: weights snap between 300/400/700/900. Use a variable font for the smooth pump.
Karaoke `times` where word i+1 starts before word i ends: the fills overlap; that is fine for fast speech.
Two words of very different width in the same slot: the line jumps. Centre it and give the sentence room.
Roll faster than 0.8 s per word: nobody reads it.
Fewer than 4 words: the ring looks sparse; add blanks.
Reading speed: each word is the centre word for `every − move` seconds.
Real photos from the network: use local images in the avatars' `label` HTML (the `no-network` gate).
Fewer than 5 avatars: the ring shows the same face twice.
Sources with no space to curve: set `curve` to 0.15.
Drawing straight lines between far-apart points: keep the default curve for the "flow" feel.
One long card text: cards are fixed-size; keep it to a few words.
Six or more cards: deep slots fade out (between slots 3 and 5).
The element has an id: clones drop it, but anything that looks it up by id still finds only the lead.
`pose` that uses clocks or `Math.random`: it must be a pure function of t.
Over 12 cards: the grid cells shrink and the ring crowds.
No `at` from `W()`: the first card falls before the word.
A shadow on a light film: it is black at 55 %; lower the opacity in CSS if needed.
Passing `el` that is not absolutely positioned: the translate has no effect on layout.
Brand logos you may not use: tiles take text; put your own SVG in `label` HTML.
More than 8 nodes: the ring gets crowded.
Pressing the first or last row without checking: the squash is one-sided; that is correct but check the look.
Too many rows: neighbours beyond two barely move.
A colour as a name with `drop-shadow`: it works, but a hex lets you tune the glow.
Two neon frames at once with different colours: filter stacks; keep one.
More than 3 laps: the tail wraps over itself.
A drop of less than 0.4 s: the bounce is invisible.
Real screenshots from the network: put local images in the cards.
A wall behind small text: it is busy; dim it with a scrim.
Real prices or product names: label them "Illustrative data".
Skipping the skeleton: without it the first frame is an empty card.
`speed` too slow: the last chips arrive after the voice moved on. Compute it from the voice: `farthest / (spokenDuration)`.
Chips over 90 px on 9:16: they collide on the inner ring.
Too few cards (under 4): the scroll ends at once.
Dense body text: the cards are small; two lines at most.
A long embed text: the card has a fixed height (`embedH`).
Setting the row's `height` yourself: the helper owns it.
Made-up values without the "Illustrative data" label.
A `max` smaller than a value: the bar passes the tile top.
Cells passed as `cells: [{ c, r, cs, rs }]` that overlap: the helper does not check.
A wireframe over a busy photo: the outlines vanish.
